questions.q: Two molecules of propanenitrile undergo the Thorpe reaction with a strong base. The product (enamine form) is:
questions.explain: The carbanion forms on the CH₂ next to C≡N and adds to the nitrile carbon of the second molecule; nothing is lost, and the imine tautomerises to the conjugated enamine.

questions.q: Which nitrile can act only as the electrophile, never as the carbanion donor, in a Thorpe reaction?
questions.explain: Benzonitrile has no α-hydrogen, so no carbanion can form from it.

questions.q: Hexanedinitrile, NC(CH₂)₄CN, is treated with base and the product is then heated with H₃O⁺. The final product is:
questions.explain: Thorpe–Ziegler ring closure gives 2-aminocyclopent-1-ene-1-carbonitrile; hydrolysis gives a β-keto acid, which loses CO₂ to leave the five-membered ketone.

questions.q: Why is a strong base such as LDA needed to form a nitrile carbanion, rather than aqueous OH⁻?
options: Nitriles are hydrolysed instantly by OH⁻ to amides
The α-H of a simple nitrile has a pKa of about 25, far less acidic than a ketone α-H
The nitrile carbanion is unstabilised by nitrogen
questions.explain: Nitrile α-hydrogens are weak acids, similar to esters (ketones about 19), so strong dry bases are needed; the negative charge is shared with N.
